interpretation: Only the previously cancelled Linux job was rerun through the job-specific GitHub API. It used the same source, five-minute limit, official package installation and existing tiny paused-QEMU mechanism. No package source, network setting or timeout was changed.

The second Linux execution passed all 1,013 tests, completed package installation, and observed paused owned QEMU with stable mapped backing-file hashes and separate local package metadata/integrity agreement. It observed process exit, control closure and work removal without forced kill.
The mapped backing-file and local package agreement do not attest resident process bytes or equivalence to upstream source. No guest, packet egress or Windows AC pair ran in that mechanism.

GitHub carries the prior successful Windows job into attempt 2 with a new job-record ID, but retains its original 11:40:37–11:42:30 execution timestamps. Windows was not rerun. Its 28-case AC schema/mock-dispatch parity, eight-mode ZIP/PowerShell parity and existing IPv6 hosted cleanup remain the attempt-1 evidence archived separately.

The first Linux cancellation remains an immutable non-green result. Retry success does not establish the unique cause of its delayed package fetches or retroactively supply its missing cleanup/provenance evidence.

Together, the retained Windows execution and the new Linux execution satisfy this reviewed short gate. The new AC mode is still default-OFF; all new role/profile/ACL/identity/48-byte bridge integration remains pure or mocked evidence, not genuine AC-pair qualification.
No automatic further attempt is authorized by this result. Any activation wiring and real Win11 AC-pair run require separate review and root decision.
